summary.title: The SaaS CTO Security Checklist Redux
summary.one_liner: A practical, team-by-team checklist of security basics (2FA, secrets management, dependency tracking, backups, logging, hiring a security engineer) that a SaaS CTO can apply to harden the company and product.
keywords: when to hire first security engineer
takeaways: Start with employee basics: 2FA everywhere, locked computers, encrypted laptops and phones, no shared accounts, and a password manager.
Build security into code review, secrets handling, and the SDLC, using SAST/DAST and dependency scanning while expecting false positives.
Harden infrastructure: test backups, isolate databases on private networks, keep OS and Docker images patched, enforce HTTPS and security headers, and centralize logs with synced clocks.
Hire a dedicated security engineer only after the engineering team has bought into security and is overwhelmed, not too early.
summary.summary: The page is a checklist organized into four areas: your employees, your code, your application, your infrastructure, and your company. Each item gives a short rationale and a set of recommended practices, followed by "Read more" links to external docs and vendor guides. It explicitly says the list is not exhaustive and depends on the company's product and assets. Most items are general advice rather than step-by-step instructions, and many tools are named as examples rather than compared in depth.
